papers.abstract_en: The Advanced Camera (AdvCam) upgrade of the Large-Sized Telescopes (LSTs) calls for a fully digital readout in which each front-end board streams data to the event-building servers over commercial 10 Gb/s Ethernet, using an FPGA implementation of Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over Converged Ethernet v2 (RoCEv2). In a previous work, a customized RoCEv2 core integrated with the SLAC SURF UDP/MAC stack was shown to sustain near-line-rate data transfers from a Xilinx KCU105 to a server equipped with a Mellanox ConnectX-5 NIC. However, the AdvCam topology is an incast funnel: many 10 GbE links converge onto a single uplink, and bare Priority Flow Control (PFC) congestion management protocol is known to be unfair and to suffer from head-of-line blocking. This work extends the previous design with the Data Center Quantized Congestion Notification (DCQCN) algorithm. A protocol-level ns-3 simulation is used to validate the DCQCN dynamics and to explore the parameter space; an FPGA rate-limiter integrated into the SURF MAC reacts to incoming Congestion Notification Packets (CNPs) according to the DCQCN state machine; a cocotb testbench with an emulated Python switch verifies the firmware end-to-end against a Soft-RoCE receiver; and a three-sender incast hardware test on a DCQCN-enabled commercial switch reproduces the canonical fair-share, reactive-redistribution, and saw-tooth behaviour expected from a commercial RDMA NIC. The internal rate-limiter register is shown to track the measured RoCEv2 throughput cycle by cycle.

papers.abstract_en: We study quaternionic polynomials whose coefficients may occur on both sides of the variable, using their degree in the four real coordinates. Such polynomials can have no roots, or many more isolated roots than their degree. A simple root has an invertible real derivative, and its sign is the sign of that derivative's determinant.   For a radial family, the roots over a non-real target reduce to one real equation. We obtain a sharp root bound and follow a change in the signed root count as roots escape to infinity.   The main results concern spherical root sets for which the polynomial derivative is invertible in the two normal directions. Under a small polynomial perturbation, a sphere splits into simple roots corresponding to the zeros of a tangent vector field, when the derivative of that field is invertible at every zero. We obtain a sharp bound in terms of the perturbation degree and a signed count of two or of minus two.   For even degrees, the construction yields polynomials with a single leading power and lower-degree terms whose simple root counts, divided by the fourth power of the degree, tend to one as the degree grows. An explicit quartic has 132 simple roots, and this count persists under small coefficient perturbations. For gradient perturbations, the roots correspond to equilibrium directions of an energy on the sphere. This correspondence gives energy thresholds for root disappearance and bounds the critical directions of polynomial orientation profiles in diffusion magnetic resonance imaging.

papers.abstract_en: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

papers.abstract_en: This paper proposes a square-root clustered Lasso penalized method for high-dimensional linear regression. By integrating square-root loss with the clustered Lasso penalty, the resulting method enables flexible regression modeling and allows tuning parameter selection independent of the unknown noise level. We establish weak decomposability of the clustered Lasso penalty and a noise-level-free tuning strategy under Gaussian noise. Furthermore, we establish the finite-sample prediction accuracy guarantees for the proposed method. The inherent nonsmoothness of the square-root loss and clustered Lasso penalty poses considerable computational difficulties. To resolve this issue, we develop an efficient semismooth Newton-based proximal augmented Lagrangian algorithm (N-ALM) to solve the corresponding dual optimization problem. The subproblems arising in the iteration are efficiently tackled by the semismooth Newton method, which fully utilizes the sparsity structure of the generalized Jacobian. We further establish global convergence and a local linear rate for the distance to the KKT solution set under suitable conditions; the local rate becomes superlinear when the penalty parameter tends to infinity. We conduct numerical experiments on real-world datasets to evaluate the computational performance of N-ALM. The results demonstrate that N-ALM solves the tested high-dimensional SRCL problems accurately and substantially reduces running times compared with d-ADMM.

papers.abstract_en: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The results do not resolve the unrestricted clique-target problem.

papers.abstract_en: Structured sparse learning is a leading paradigm for high-dimensional data modeling, as it enables rigorous integration of domain-validated structural priors into the learning process. Among these priors, pre-defined grouped structure and piecewise smoothness are ubiquitous in real-world applications. However, most existing structured regularization methods are built on squared loss and convex penalties, rarely jointly model these two complementary structural priors, and suffer from two key limitations. Their optimal tuning parameters are sensitive to the unknown noise level $σ$ due to the squared loss. Meanwhile, convex penalties induce inherent estimation bias and severe over-shrinkage of large magnitudes. To address these issues, we propose a knowledge-driven Nonconvex Structured Smooth Adjustment for Square-Root Regularization (NS$^3$R), which unifies the $σ$-free square-root loss with a joint nonconvex $\ell_{2,q}$ penalty ($0 < q < 1$) to simultaneously encode group sparsity and structured smoothness priors. Theoretically, we establish rigorous non-asymptotic error bounds for the NS$^3$R estimator under a mild $(2,q)$-group restricted compatibility condition. Computationally, we develop an efficient double-screened IRLS with thresholding (DS-IRLS-th) algorithm, which adopts a nested double-screening strategy to reduce computational cost and improve numerical stability, with provable global convergence for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate that NS$^3$R consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in finite-sample settings.

papers.abstract_en: Causal relativistic hydrodynamics introduces relaxation degrees of freedom that elevate a quadratic oscillation problem to a cubic non-Hermitian spectral pencil. We study its exceptional-point (EP2) curves and an $A_3$ cusp, and construct an exactly solvable radiating wave--relaxation problem with a Pöschl--Teller potential and an Israel--Stewart channel. Using hyperboloidal coordinates, outgoing Siegert conditions become endpoint conditions. For the aligned transport profile and away from discrete resonant couplings, we prove that the complete quasinormal point spectrum decomposes into a tower of sector cubics, with radiative damping rates determined by the boundary-value problem. The resulting EP2 and cusp geometry is therefore realized by genuine quasinormal eigenvalues. Multiprecision bordered-Newton calculations certify the degeneracies and their square-root and cubic-root splitting laws. Under a controlled parity-preserving deformation of the viscosity profile, the fundamental EP2 survives over a finite parameter window before annihilating with a partner and moving into complexified parameters; the cusp also persists. For dense matter, we derive a criterion independent of the relaxation time: $(v_{\rm FR}/v_β)^2 \ge 1+Θ(γ)$, where $Θ(γ)$ is the minimum coupling ratio along the EP2 locus. For weakly radiating compressive modes, $Θ\simeq 8$, requiring $v_{\rm FR}\gtrsim 3v_β$. Internally consistent nucleonic Urca matter misses this threshold by more than two orders of magnitude. Exotic-matter comparisons are indicative benchmarks rather than same-equation-of-state exclusions. The radiating model is not a relativistic TOV-star perturbation; establishing the mechanism in a realistic star remains open.

papers.abstract_en: Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.

papers.abstract_en: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $Γ$ its long-root geometry, namely $Γ$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $Γ$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $Γ$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $Γ$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $Γ$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $Γ$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $Γ$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $Γ$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

papers.abstract_en: We study Frobenius intersection profiles of maximum rank distance (MRD) codes arising from ordinary polynomial multiples over finite fields. We prove that every numerically admissible profile is realized within this family over every sufficiently large extension, using a root-exponent pattern independent of the extension degree. A factor-orbit gap formula provides the underlying structural description, while effective extension-degree bounds guarantee realization. We also establish a lower bound valid for all polynomial generators and show that the upper and lower bounds differ by only $O_q(\log n)$ along an infinite family of parameters. Finally, we characterize the generalized Gabidulin members and obtain non-generalized-Gabidulin realizations of every profile with initial loss at least two over infinitely many extensions.

papers.abstract_en: Recovering from failures in long-horizon, stateful language agents is challenging because the action introducing a defect, the symptom exposing it, and the persistent state requiring repair frequently diverge. Existing methods largely focus on retrospective failure attribution, leaving sequential diagnosis and state repair poorly integrated under constrained budgets. We introduce TRACE-FIX, a unified recovery framework centered on versioned residual task state. Trace transforms execution logs into a structured dependency-linked ledger, prioritizing unresolved task requirements rather than salient surface errors. Fix formulates recovery as budgeted planning over admissible actions, incorporating outcome forecasting and explicit repair-reserve constraints to prevent premature budget exhaustion. To rigorously decouple localization accuracy from downstream repair capability, we present LongH-Debug, evaluating root-cause attribution, verified-fault recovery, and end-to-end closed-loop execution independently. Our empirical analysis demonstrates that structured residual tracking substantially improves causal localization over raw-trace baselines, while budget-aware sequential planning converts verified fault signals into more reliable task recovery without destructive trial-and-error. Code is available at https://github.com/toffeecat/tracedp.

papers.abstract_en: Modals such as may and must can take on different senses depending on discourse context, alternating between root interpretations (e.g., permission, obligation) and epistemic interpretations (e.g., knowledge, belief). While modals are known to be notoriously difficult for children to acquire, limited research exists on whether language models (LMs) can reliably distinguish between different modal senses. We evaluate seven LMs that vary in architecture, size, and training data type using vector-based similarity and surprisal measures across four datasets. Specifically, we investigate whether LMs can leverage contextual information to disambiguate modal senses and whether their performance reflects the distribution of modal senses in their training data. We show that larger LMs trained on diverse text successfully leverage additional contextual information when available. In the absence of context, they tend to favor the dominant sense based on corpus statistics. Smaller developmentally plausible LMs, including those trained on child-directed language (CDL), fail to show consistent sensitivity to modal sense distinctions and do not benefit from context to the same degree.

papers.abstract_en: We prove that the complete flag manifold SU(m)/T m-1, with m >= 3 and its standard complex structure, admits no invariant Hermitian metric with constant mixed Chern curvature when the coefficient of the holomorphic sectional curvature is nonzero. This extends the preceding nonexistence result for a particular Wallach metric on SU(3)/T2 to all invariant Hermitian metrics and to complete type-A flags of arbitrary dimension. Curvature evaluations on holomorphic root spheres contradict a necessary trace identity, covering both Kahler and non-Kahler invariant metrics and excluding both zero and nonzero curvature constants.
